$comment: What any good explanation of this PR says, written by a model from the PR's title, description and diff only (scripts/eval-assertions.ts). The eval grades each run against them. Delete one that is wrong; keep them stable so evals compare.

assertions.text: Says that the change lets staff hide a product variant in a single channel via a flag, without deleting the listing or its prices.
Says that a listing flagged unavailable is treated as if it did not exist for customers, e.g. availability, price range, checkout and order lines, promotions.
Says that a non-nullable boolean is_available_for_purchase, defaulting to true, is added to ProductVariantChannelListing, with a migration.
Says that a new mutation toggles availability for several channels of one variant, identified by ID or SKU, and requires manage-products permission.
Says that the toggle mutation errors with not found when the variant has no listing in a requested channel, instead of creating price-less listings.
Says that sellability is centralized, as a queryset filter and an in-Python property, requiring both a price and the availability flag, replacing scattered price-not-null checks.
Says that the toggle locks listing rows with select-for-update, and only for changed flags marks products dirty and emits a variant-updated event.
Says that new listings created without the flag, or with null, default to available, while updates that omit it keep the stored value.
Does not claim that setting the flag to false deletes the channel listing or clears its price.
Does not claim that the toggle mutation is the only way to set the flag; bulk create, bulk update and the listing update input also accept it.
